source.quote: SMSL's own page for the C200, read 2026-11-27 with curl, « Introduction » bullets: « ESS Technology high-end D/A chip ES9038Q2M; »; « The 2nd generation XMOS solution supports DoP64 and native DSD512, and PCM supports up to 32bit/768kHz; »; « Input ports (except Bluetooth) support DSD transmission, coaxial and optical supports DoP64; »; « Qualcomm latest Bluetooth chip supports LDAC 24bit/96kHz, APTX/HD, SBC, AAC; »

facts.chip: ESS ES9038Q2M (« ESS Technology high-end D/A chip ES9038Q2M »).

_the_ceiling_is_the_XMOS_bullet: The rate and DSD ceilings come from the bullet naming the XMOS USB receiver, so they are written on usb only. No other input is given a PCM rate: the page states none.
_optical_has_DoP64_and_no_rate: Optical and coaxial get DoP64 from the maker's own clause and no PCM ceiling, because none is stated: copying 768 kHz onto optical is the error vocabulary/why-the-optical-default-stays-low.json exists to prevent.
_DoP64_ON_USB_IS_WHAT_THE_PAGE_SAYS: « supports DoP64 and native DSD512 » on USB, where the DO100 and SU-6 pages - same chip family, same bullet otherwise word for word - say « DoP256 ». It may be a typo on this page; it is recorded as written, because the alternative is correcting a maker from its sister product, which is the inference this catalogue refuses. A consumer told DoP64 on USB will send native DSD instead, which this page says works to DSD512.
